purpose: machine_readable knowledge-searcher subdomain KB for locating, retrieving, evaluating, and synthesizing authoritative knowledge on visual design principles and the history of design, modeled as concrete evaluable work units.
assumptions: scope is visual design principles and design history within the parent domain Design: Fashion, Architecture & Principles
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
nodes are concrete design-principles and design-history work units, not abstract themes
audience is a model orchestrating where and how to find and evaluate design knowledge

competency_questions.question: What is the communicative intent and audience this design must serve?
How will viewers perceptually group and parse the elements?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GESTALT and hierarchy nodes define grouping

competency_questions.question: What is seen first and how is the eye led through the design?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: hierarchy, balance, and contrast nodes resolve focal flow

competency_questions.question: What grid and spacing system gives the layout order and rhythm?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: grid and contrast nodes specify the system

competency_questions.question: How is the layout composed to fit the intent and format?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: composition node maps focal flow and negative space

competency_questions.question: What palette and harmony scheme carry the intended mood?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: color node defines palette roles and harmony

competency_questions.question: Does the color system meet accessibility and contrast requirements?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: accessibility node verifies contrast and CVD safety

competency_questions.question: What typefaces and setting deliver the right voice and readability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: type nodes define selection and setting

competency_questions.question: How is the tension between form, function, ornament, and style resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: form-function and style nodes record the stance

competency_questions.question: Where does a movement sit in design history and what did it stand for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: history nodes place and characterize movements

competency_questions.question: How do historical principles apply to or misfit a current context?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: modernism and form-function nodes weigh fit

competency_questions.question: How is a design-history claim sourced and judged for reliability?
How is a design evaluated against intent and principles rather than taste?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: critique node ties points to intent and principles

competency_questions.question: What documented system is locked and handed off as the reusable artifact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: spec node produces the documented system after gates

glossary.definition: the ranking of elements by importance using size, weight, position, and contrast
perceptual grouping laws such as proximity, similarity, closure, and figure-ground
a structure of columns, rows, and margins that orders layout and spacing
a relationship among hues, values, and saturations that feels coherent
the measured luminance difference between text and background for accessibility
the line length of set text, a key readability variable
the categorization of typefaces by anatomy and historical style
the International Typographic Style emphasizing grids, sans-serif type, and objectivity
the German school uniting art, craft, and industry with functional, geometric design
a reaction against modernist rules favoring expression, irony, and historical reference
a style reducing a design to its essential elements
the debate over whether appearance should follow purpose

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established design-principles and design-history practice and canonical texts (Lupton & Phillips Graphic Design: The New Basics; Hollis Graphic Design: A Concise History; Munari Design as Art).

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix what a design must communicate, to whom, and the single intended viewer response before any visual decision.
contradictors: designer who styles with no brief

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when audience, medium, or message changes

pros.claim: every visual choice inherits one clear communicative goal
pros.example: a poster for teens differs from an annual-report cover

cons.claim: a wrong intent misdirects the whole composition
cons.example: setting a playful look the client wanted authoritative

failure_modes: intent stated as a topic not a response
acceptance_tests: intent is one sentence naming a viewer response
brief names audience and medium

nodes.definition: Apply grouping laws (proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, figure-ground) that govern how viewers parse a layout.
contradictors: decorator who ignores grouping

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when grouping is misread in testing

pros.claim: viewers parse structure pre-attentively without instructions
pros.example: cards spaced into clear clusters read as one set each

cons.claim: violated laws create unintended associations
cons.example: tight spacing fuses two unrelated buttons

acceptance_tests: related items group by proximity or similarity
figure and ground are unambiguous

nodes.definition: Rank elements by importance and steer the eye with size, weight, position, and contrast toward the primary message.
contradictors: maximalist who emphasizes everything

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the primary message is not seen first

pros.claim: the most important thing is seen first
pros.example: a headline dominates while metadata recedes

cons.claim: flat hierarchy buries the message
cons.example: every block shouting equally reads as noise

acceptance_tests: one dominant focal point exists
reading order matches priority

nodes.definition: Distribute visual weight across the composition for symmetric, asymmetric, or radial equilibrium that fits the intent.
contradictors: designer who only centers everything

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a layout feels lopsided or unstable

pros.claim: a stable field lets the eye rest where intended
pros.example: an asymmetric layout feels dynamic yet controlled

cons.claim: accidental imbalance distracts from content
cons.example: a heavy lower-left corner drags the eye off-message

acceptance_tests: weight reads as intentional not accidental
balance type matches the brief tone
revisit_triggers: element added or removed shifts weight

nodes.definition: Use a grid plus alignment and proximity to create order, connection, and consistent spatial relationships.
contradictors: freeform designer who rejects grids

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the grid is broken or content reflows

pros.claim: order and rhythm emerge from a repeatable structure
pros.example: a 12-column grid keeps a long page coherent

cons.claim: a rigid grid can flatten expression
cons.example: forcing every image to the grid kills a hero moment

acceptance_tests: every element aligns to a grid line or edge
related items sit closer than unrelated ones
revisit_triggers: content reflows to a new breakpoint

nodes.definition: Use contrast to differentiate, repetition to unify, and rhythm to pace the eye across the composition.
contradictors: designer who avoids all contrast

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the design reads monotonous or chaotic

pros.claim: contrast clarifies roles while repetition binds a system
pros.example: consistent button styling unifies a whole interface

cons.claim: overused contrast becomes visual noise
cons.example: every word bold defeats the point of bold

failure_modes: weak contrast that fails to differentiate
acceptance_tests: contrast is sufficient to differentiate roles
repeated elements unify the set

nodes.definition: Build palettes from color relationships (hue, value, saturation, temperature, harmony schemes) that serve mood and legibility.
contradictors: designer who picks colors at random

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when palette fails mood or accessibility checks

pros.claim: a structured palette sets mood and guides attention
pros.example: an analogous scheme feels calm and cohesive

cons.claim: poor value contrast breaks legibility regardless of hue
cons.example: two same-value colors vibrate and tire the eye

acceptance_tests: palette has a defined role for each color
value contrast supports legibility
revisit_triggers: palette fails a mood or brand check

nodes.definition: Verify color choices meet contrast and color-vision-deficiency requirements so meaning never relies on hue alone.
contradictors: designer who ignores accessibility

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a contrast or CVD audit fails

pros.claim: the design works for low-vision and color-blind users
pros.example: adding icons beside color states keeps meaning intact

cons.claim: strict contrast can constrain an expressive palette
cons.example: an aesthetic pastel set fails text-contrast minimums

acceptance_tests: text contrast meets the target ratio
meaning is not conveyed by hue alone

nodes.definition: Select and pair typefaces using type anatomy, classification, and voice that match the message and audience.
contradictors: designer who uses one default font

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when typeface voice misfits the brand

pros.claim: type carries voice before a word is read
pros.example: a humanist sans signals warmth and approachability

cons.claim: a wrong voice undermines the message
cons.example: a playful display face on a legal notice erodes trust

acceptance_tests: typefaces match the intended voice
pairings have clear contrast of role

nodes.definition: Set text for readability with measure, leading, tracking, hierarchy, and a modular type scale.
contradictors: designer who ignores measure and leading

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reading comfort fails in testing

pros.claim: comfortable reading keeps the audience in the content
pros.example: a 60-character measure with generous leading reads easily

cons.claim: tight setting saves space at the cost of comprehension
cons.example: jamming more words per line slows reading

acceptance_tests: line length sits in a readable measure
leading and scale support comfortable reading

nodes.definition: Compose elements into a layout using framing, focal flow, negative space, and proportion systems toward the intent.
contradictors: designer who places elements ad hoc

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the layout fails to lead the eye

pros.claim: a composed layout delivers the message in the intended order
pros.example: a strong diagonal flow pulls the eye to the call-to-action

cons.claim: weak composition wastes strong individual elements
cons.example: good photos lost in a cluttered, pathless page

acceptance_tests: focal flow follows the intended reading path
negative space is intentional
revisit_triggers: layout fails to lead the eye

nodes.definition: Select and treat imagery, illustration, and icons so style, meaning, and consistency support the message.
contradictors: designer who pulls images with no system

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when imagery style drifts from the system

pros.claim: a consistent visual language reinforces the brand
pros.example: a single duotone treatment unifies stock photos

cons.claim: inconsistent imagery fragments the system
cons.example: mixing flat and skeuomorphic icons looks unplanned

acceptance_tests: imagery shares a consistent treatment
icons read clearly at target size
revisit_triggers: imagery style drifts from the system

nodes.definition: Resolve the tension between form and function and decide where ornament earns its place versus where it distracts.
contradictors: dogmatist for or against ornament

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when decoration overrides usability or vice versa

pros.claim: intentional restraint or expression matches the message
pros.example: a Swiss-style report stays clean while a poster can be lush

cons.claim: ideology applied blindly misfits the context
cons.example: stripping all ornament from a festive flyer kills its mood

acceptance_tests: each decorative choice has a communicative or brand reason
function is never sacrificed to ornament

nodes.definition: Map the chronological arc of design from craft and Arts-and-Crafts through industrial and digital eras as shared context.
contradictors: practitioner who ignores history

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a movement is misdated or miscredited

pros.claim: a shared timeline lets references be placed and reasoned about
pros.example: knowing Bauhaus precedes Swiss style explains the lineage

cons.claim: a tidy timeline can flatten parallel non-Western design
cons.example: an Anglo-Euro arc omits Japanese and Soviet contributions

acceptance_tests: movements are placed in correct relative order
each era links to a driving cause

nodes.definition: Characterize modernist design—Bauhaus, De Stijl, the International Typographic (Swiss) Style—and its grid-and-function principles.
contradictors: designer who treats modernism as the only canon

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a movement's tenets are misattributed

pros.claim: modernist principles underpin much of contemporary practice
pros.example: Swiss grid and Helvetica shaped corporate identity systems

cons.claim: treating modernism as a universal default ignores context
cons.example: forcing minimal Swiss style onto an expressive cultural brand

acceptance_tests: named figures and tenets are correct
grid-and-sans lineage is traced accurately
revisit_triggers: style misapplied to a misfit context

nodes.definition: Characterize postmodern, punk, deconstructivist, and revival reactions against modernist rules and their expressive logic.
contradictors: purist who rejects all postmodern work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a reaction is read as mere noise not intent

pros.claim: understanding reactions explains expressive and rule-breaking work
pros.example: grunge typography reads as deliberate once its roots are known

cons.claim: rule-breaking without grounding looks like incompetence
cons.example: layering noise with no concept just confuses readers

failure_modes: reviving a style without its meaning
acceptance_tests: each reaction is tied to what it opposed
expressive intent is distinguished from chaos
revisit_triggers: a reaction read as mere noise

nodes.definition: Track how styles evolve—minimalism, flat, skeuomorphism, neumorphism, maximalism—and when each fits a context.
contradictors: designer who copies the current trend blindly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a trend is adopted without fit

pros.claim: style is chosen for fit not fashion
pros.example: flat design suits a content-dense dashboard

cons.claim: chasing trends dates a design fast
cons.example: neumorphism that fails contrast harms usability

acceptance_tests: chosen style fits the audience and platform
trend choice is justified beyond fashion

nodes.definition: Use signs, symbols, and denotation/connotation so visual elements carry the intended meaning across the target culture.
contradictors: designer who ignores cultural reading

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a symbol reads differently in the target culture

pros.claim: deliberate signs communicate meaning beyond the literal
pros.example: a green check reads as success across most contexts

cons.claim: a symbol can carry an unintended cultural meaning
cons.example: a gesture or color that is positive in one culture and negative in another

failure_modes: a symbol with an unintended cultural meaning
acceptance_tests: each symbol's intended meaning is stated
cultural connotations are checked
revisit_triggers: a symbol carries the wrong connotation

nodes.definition: Evaluate a design against intent, principles, and audience using structured critique and evidence rather than taste.
contradictors: reviewer who critiques on taste alone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when critique drifts to subjective taste

pros.claim: critique tied to intent yields actionable revisions
pros.example: noting weak hierarchy against the stated goal beats I-do-not-like-it

cons.claim: subjective critique stalls progress and demoralizes
cons.example: endless taste debates with no criteria block decisions

failure_modes: critique with no link to intent
acceptance_tests: each critique point ties to intent or a principle
evidence beyond opinion is cited

nodes.definition: Locate and judge authoritative design knowledge—canonical books, archives, attributions—and weigh their reliability.
contradictors: writer who asserts history without sources

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an attribution or claim cannot be sourced

pros.claim: grounded claims survive scrutiny and update cleanly
pros.example: citing Hollis for a movement date beats a blog assertion

cons.claim: canon books carry their own biases and gaps
cons.example: relying on one Western survey omits whole traditions

failure_modes: over-reliance on a single biased source
acceptance_tests: each historical claim has a locatable source
attributions are corroborated

nodes.definition: Lock the system into a documented spec—principles, palette, type, grid, usage—as a reusable handoff artifact.
contradictors: team that ships with no documented system

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the spec ships before critique or accessibility passes

pros.claim: a documented system makes design reproducible and consistent
pros.example: a style guide lets new contributors stay on-brand

cons.claim: locking too early freezes unresolved problems
cons.example: shipping a spec with failing contrast spreads the defect

acceptance_tests: spec documents principles, palette, type, grid, and usage
all gates passed before lock
revisit_triggers: new component added to the system

edges.why_related: intent frames what must be grouped and seen
edges.example: clustering nav vs content by purpose

edges.why_related: intent sets which message ranks first
edges.example: headline chosen by communicative goal

edges.why_related: grouping must exist before emphasis can rank groups
edges.example: emphasize a cluster only once it reads as one

edges.why_related: weight is distributed around the focal hierarchy
edges.risk_of_conflict: balancing without hierarchy hides the focus
edges.example: heavier focal element offset by space

edges.why_related: proximity grouping is realized through a grid
edges.risk_of_conflict: grid without grouping logic looks arbitrary
edges.example: columns spaced to group modules

edges.why_related: balance targets are met within the grid structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: grid set before balance fights it
edges.example: margins tuned for visual balance

edges.why_related: contrast realizes the planned emphasis
edges.example: bold weight marks the top of hierarchy

edges.why_related: rhythm is paced along grid intervals
edges.example: repeating modules on a baseline grid

edges.why_related: intent sets the mood the palette must carry
edges.risk_of_conflict: palette built before mood is set drifts
edges.example: calm palette for a wellness brand

edges.why_related: accessibility is checked on the chosen palette
edges.example: verifying text contrast on brand colors

edges.why_related: intent sets the voice type must carry
edges.risk_of_conflict: type chosen before voice is set misfits
edges.example: humanist sans for a warm brand

edges.why_related: setting rules depend on the chosen typeface
edges.risk_of_conflict: setting before face is chosen is redone
edges.example: leading tuned to x-height

edges.why_related: measure and columns derive from the grid
edges.example: column width caps line length

edges.why_related: composition arranges the ranked elements
edges.risk_of_conflict: composing without ranks loses the path
edges.example: focal flow follows the hierarchy

edges.why_related: layout is built on the grid structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: ad hoc layout drifts off grid
edges.example: placing modules on grid lines

edges.why_related: composition must satisfy balance targets
edges.example: offsetting a heavy image with space

edges.why_related: imagery is selected to fit the composition
edges.risk_of_conflict: images chosen before layout get cropped badly
edges.example: hero image sized to the focal area

edges.why_related: image treatment follows the palette
edges.example: duotone images in brand colors

edges.why_related: semiotic meaning is assigned to the chosen imagery and icons
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading meaning before elements exist is moot
edges.example: a chosen icon's connotation is then checked
edges.resolution_rule: select imagery before reading its meaning

edges.why_related: the movement sits within the timeline
edges.example: Bauhaus dated to the 1920s
edges.resolution_rule: place the era before detailing it

edges.why_related: reactions are defined against modernism
edges.risk_of_conflict: reaction without its target is unclear
edges.example: postmodernism reacts to Swiss rigidity

edges.why_related: sourcing supports the timeline's claims
edges.example: citing a history for a date

edges.why_related: style evolution is read along the timeline
edges.risk_of_conflict: trend with no lineage looks random
edges.example: flat design as a reaction to skeuomorphism

edges.why_related: the form-function stance frames style choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: style picked with no stance drifts
edges.example: minimalism justified by function
edges.resolution_rule: take a stance before picking a style

edges.why_related: critique evaluates the composed layout
edges.example: reviewing the composed page against intent

edges.why_related: readability is part of the critique
edges.example: testing the measure in critique

edges.why_related: the spec is locked only after critique passes
edges.example: gate the system on a passed critique

edges.why_related: the spec encodes the accessible palette
edges.risk_of_conflict: spec with failing contrast spreads defects
edges.example: documenting contrast-passing tokens

edges.why_related: the spec documents the type system
edges.example: tokenizing the type scale

edges.why_related: the spec documents image and icon rules
edges.example: icon usage rules in the guide

edges.why_related: the spec encodes contrast and repetition rules
edges.example: button repetition rules in the guide

edges.why_related: accessibility bounds the harmony choices
edges.example: a pastel pair forced to meet contrast
edges.resolution_rule: accessibility minimums bound the palette; adjust value not abandon harmony

edges.why_related: the ornament policy limits decorative layout moves
edges.example: trimming decorative rules that hurt flow
edges.resolution_rule: function bounds ornament; drop decoration that harms the path

edges.why_related: source quality changes the accuracy of movement claims
edges.example: correcting a misattributed Bauhaus figure
edges.resolution_rule: prefer corroborated sources over single survey

edges.why_related: history shapes how the form-ornament debate is framed
edges.example: Loos' ornament critique informs the policy
edges.resolution_rule: ground the stance in historical debate

edges.why_related: style choice should precede imagery treatment
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating images before style is set is redone
edges.example: flat icons chosen after picking flat style

edges.why_related: critique can trigger a revisit of hierarchy
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring critique entrenches a weak focus
edges.example: critique reorders a buried headline
edges.resolution_rule: revisit hierarchy when critique flags it; stop when the focal test passes

edges.why_related: critique can trigger a revisit of the palette
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring critique keeps a clashing palette
edges.example: critique flags a muddy palette
edges.resolution_rule: revisit palette when critique flags it; stop when mood and contrast pass

edges.why_related: balance and composition are closely related spatial concerns
edges.example: both reason about where weight sits
edges.resolution_rule: treat as related but keep balance and layout as distinct steps

edges.why_related: contrast and emphasis overlap as differentiation tools
edges.example: both differentiate elements
edges.resolution_rule: treat as related; emphasis ranks, contrast differentiates

conflict_axes.trigger: an expressive choice degrades usability or legibility
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: usability and legibility floors dominate expression; expression is maximized only above the floor
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no expressive option meets the accessibility floor
conflict_axes.example: a moody low-contrast palette that fails text legibility

conflict_axes.trigger: a strong creative moment wants to break the grid
resolution_order: allow a deliberate break for a hero moment
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the grid dominates by default; breaks are allowed only as deliberate, documented exceptions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if breaks accumulate and the system loses coherence
conflict_axes.example: a full-bleed hero image breaking a strict 12-column grid

conflict_axes.trigger: reducing elements removes needed affordances or character
resolution_order: keep elements that carry meaning or affordance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: meaning and affordance dominate; minimalism removes only redundant elements, never necessary ones
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if minimalism hides a required affordance
conflict_axes.example: a flat UI that hides which elements are clickable

conflict_axes.trigger: applying universal modernist rules misfits a specific culture or message
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: audience and context fit dominate canonical defaults; the canon informs but does not dictate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a canonical default actively alienates the audience
conflict_axes.example: forcing minimalist Swiss style onto an expressive cultural festival brand

conflict_axes.trigger: a current trend conflicts with the longevity the brief needs
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: required longevity dominates trend appeal; trends are adopted only where refresh cost is acceptable
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a trend would date a long-lived brand quickly
conflict_axes.example: neumorphism on a brand expected to last a decade

conflict_axes.trigger: a harmonious low-contrast palette fails accessibility ratios
resolution_order: raise value contrast where text sits
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accessibility contrast dominates harmony for functional text; harmony leads only for decorative areas
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no value adjustment preserves both harmony and contrast
conflict_axes.example: an analogous pastel scheme that fails body-text contrast

conflict_axes.trigger: a deadline pressures locking the spec before critique and audits pass
resolution_order: run the critique and accessibility gates
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: critique and accessibility gates dominate speed; the spec cannot hard-lock until they pass
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a deadline forces shipping with a failing gate
conflict_axes.example: locking a system with unreviewed, low-contrast components to hit a launch

conflict_axes.trigger: a reviewer's personal taste conflicts with intent-grounded evidence
resolution_order: ground each point in a principle or data
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: intent-grounded evidence dominates personal taste; taste is admissible only as a tie-breaker
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if taste-only objections block an evidence-supported design
conflict_axes.example: a stakeholder rejecting a tested layout because they dislike a color

edge_cases.trigger: final text fails contrast or measure checks
edge_cases.example: light-gray body text on white below 3:1
edge_cases.detection_method: run a contrast checker and measure audit on shipped text

edge_cases.trigger: elements stop aligning to the grid mid-layout
edge_cases.example: a card two pixels off the column
edge_cases.detection_method: overlay the grid and check edges against guides

edge_cases.failure_mode: the viewer has no entry point
edge_cases.example: every block the same size and weight
edge_cases.detection_method: squint test or saliency check for a single focal point

edge_cases.trigger: imagery colors clash with the palette
edge_cases.example: warm stock photos in a cool brand palette
edge_cases.detection_method: sample image colors against the palette

edge_cases.trigger: the typeface voice contradicts the message
edge_cases.example: a comic display face on a financial report
edge_cases.detection_method: compare typeface voice to the stated intent

edge_cases.trigger: a movement claim is uncited or wrong
edge_cases.detection_method: check each claim against a cited authoritative source

edge_cases.trigger: a trend is adopted that the brief's lifespan cannot afford
edge_cases.example: a fad gradient on a long-lived logo
edge_cases.detection_method: compare style durability to the required lifespan

edge_cases.trigger: the spec is hard-locked before critique and audits pass
edge_cases.failure_mode: unresolved defects spread across the system
edge_cases.example: shipping a token set with a failing contrast pair
edge_cases.detection_method: check that critique and accessibility gates passed before lock

edge_cases.failure_mode: the core message is lost in ornament
edge_cases.example: borders and textures burying a headline
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether each decorative element has a stated reason

edge_cases.trigger: elements form an accidental tangent or trap
edge_cases.failure_mode: the eye snags on an unintended edge
edge_cases.example: a horizon line just touching a head
edge_cases.detection_method: scan edges for tangents and traps

edge_cases.trigger: a derived score is labeled observed or computed inconsistently
edge_cases.failure_mode: the KB makes unsupported empirical claims
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute derived fields and re-check all labels

dominance_rules.trigger: legibility competes with an aesthetic choice
dominance_rules.rule: legibility and accessibility floors dominate aesthetic expression
dominance_rules.required_action: raise contrast or measure before sacrificing readability
dominance_rules.example: keeping body text readable over a moody low-contrast look

dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline pressures skipping a check on a risky decision
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: run the gate before shipping, never after
dominance_rules.example: auditing contrast before launch, not after

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node sits before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.required_action: place prerequisites before dependents regardless of value
dominance_rules.example: fixing intent before designing the hero layout

dominance_rules.trigger: an evidence label conflicts with a precise-looking number
dominance_rules.required_action: label estimates heuristic and keep observed fields at zero
dominance_rules.example: tagging an estimated weight heuristic not observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a spec is ready to lock but a gate has not passed
dominance_rules.rule: QA and critique gates dominate locking
dominance_rules.required_action: do not hard-lock until critique and accessibility pass
dominance_rules.example: holding the spec lock until contrast passes

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible release or high-risk node is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible or high-risk steps
dominance_rules.required_action: require human sign-off before the master is released
keep the required structure before adding more nodes
dominance_rules.example: not adding a malformed node to pad counts

dominance_rules.trigger: a history claim lacks a source
dominance_rules.required_action: cite or drop any historical claim
dominance_rules.example: citing Hollis for a movement date or removing the claim

dominance_rules.trigger: a canonical default misfits the audience
dominance_rules.rule: audience and context fit dominate canonical defaults
dominance_rules.required_action: adapt the canon to the audience with a recorded reason
dominance_rules.example: departing from Swiss minimalism for a cultural brand

dominance_rules.trigger: a taste objection conflicts with intent-grounded evidence
dominance_rules.rule: intent-grounded evidence dominates personal taste in critique
dominance_rules.required_action: resolve critique by principle and data, taste only breaks ties
dominance_rules.example: keeping a tested layout over a stakeholder's color dislike

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix intent before any visual decision
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a design for the wrong intent is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: visual choices change after intent is clarified
anti_rework_rules.example: styling a page before knowing the audience

anti_rework_rules.rule: set hierarchy before balance, grid, and composition
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a grid built for the wrong focus is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the grid is rebuilt after the focal point shifts
anti_rework_rules.example: laying a grid before deciding what leads

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the grid before composing the layout
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ad hoc layouts drift and get re-aligned later
anti_rework_rules.example: placing modules before a grid exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: build the palette before auditing accessibility
anti_rework_rules.rationale: auditing an unbuilt palette wastes effort
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: contrast is checked on placeholder colors
anti_rework_rules.example: running contrast checks before colors exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose the typeface before tuning setting
anti_rework_rules.rationale: setting tuned to the wrong face is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: leading is retuned after the face changes
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning leading before picking the font

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix color and type before composing and treating imagery
anti_rework_rules.rationale: composing before color and type forces re-treatment
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: imagery is re-treated after the palette changes
anti_rework_rules.example: sourcing imagery before the palette exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: take a form-function stance before picking a style
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a style chosen with no stance leads to trend churn
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the style is reversed after a stance is set
anti_rework_rules.example: adopting a trend before deciding form-function

anti_rework_rules.rule: source history claims before publishing them
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unsourced claims are retracted and rewritten
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a published claim cannot be backed by a source
anti_rework_rules.example: asserting a movement date with no citation

anti_rework_rules.rule: critique and audit before locking the spec
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a locked spec with defects spreads them across the system
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the spec is hard-locked before gates pass
anti_rework_rules.example: shipping a system with a failing contrast pair

anti_rework_rules.rule: produce a handoff artifact after each major step
anti_rework_rules.rationale: missing handoffs force re-derivation in later sessions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a step ends with no reusable artifact
anti_rework_rules.example: finishing composition with no documented layout
